label: 4 · Tag Navigation
info:
Tag navigation, one node per step, like the AprilTag blocks in DroneBlocks.

Every row starts with its button on the left. Everything here works in the simulator and on an aircraft; on an aircraft the pilot keeps the radio and can take over at any time by leaving Offboard.

'Forward' is relative to the drone's nose: start with the nose pointing at the next tag.

name: Tag hop: tag 0 → tag 1, and back (sim and drone)
info: Start on the ground over tag 0, nose toward tag 1. TAG HOP takes off, centers on tag 0, flies forward until tag 1 and lands on it. HOP BACK does the reverse from tag 1. Alternate them for repeat testing.

name: Corridor: tags 0 → 4 (sim and drone)
info: START takes off by itself. PILOT HAND-OFF waits for the pilot: take off by hand, hover over tag 0, flip the Offboard switch. Both join the same chain at 'center on tag 0'. Change the route by editing the tag numbers.

name: Safety
info: Any step that fails lands the aircraft where it is, but only while the mission still has it (Offboard): a step also fails when the pilot takes over, and landing then would take the aircraft from the pilot. LAND now always lands.

name: Dashboard: status, speak, camera
info: Shows the last step and the downward camera on the DEXI April Tag Navigation page, and speaks each new tag the camera sees (the dashboard must be open, and clicked once).

label: 5 · AVR 2026 Vision
info:
Two detectors light the LED ring.

YOLO publishes what it sees on `/yolo_detections`: barrels and barns.
`gasoline` is done as an example. The rest are yours.

The bar counter publishes on `/bar_detections`: how many white bars are in
the black disc of a bridge cup. All three bar counts are wired.

1. Point the camera at a printed card and watch the debug nodes to see the data.
2. Read the `pick a class` function node. It works but it is basic.
3. Add rules to the `class -> color` switch node.

name: YOLO class labels
info:
The ten strings the model can emit. Copy and paste them, a typo will not
raise an error.

```
wheat_barrel
water_barrel
gasoline
toxic_fluid
wheat_barn
water_barn
bridge_1line
bridge_2line
bridge_3line
blackout
```

The color for each one is in the AVR 2026 game manual.

Bridge cups are read better by the bar counter below. The YOLO bridge
classes are a fallback.

name: pick a class
Add the other classes
info:
`gasoline` goes out of output 1 to a red `led` node.

Add a rule per class, set the switch to that many outputs, and wire each one
to an `led` node with the right color. Check the manual for how many colors
you need.

name: Already wired
info:
`led` turns a color name into a service request and `ros2-service-call`
sends it. Every `led` node wires into this same service call node.

Colors: red green blue yellow purple cyan white orange teal magenta gold
pink aqua jade amber old_lace black. black turns the ring off.

name: Turning the ring off when detection stops
info:
Both detectors publish only when they see something, so nothing arrives on
an empty frame and the ring would hold its last color indefinitely.

Every detection restarts the timer below. When 5 seconds pass with no
detection the timer fires and the ring goes off.

The ring is shared with the flight mode indicator, which sets a color only
when the mode changes. After this clears the ring, the flight mode color
returns on the next mode change.

name: Bar counter outputs
info:
`/bar_detections` uses the same message as `/yolo_detections`.
`class_name` is one of:

```
bars_1   one white bar in a black disc
bars_2   two bars
bars_3   three bars
bars_0   plain black disc, no bars: the inactive row, ring off
```

Nothing is published when the counter cannot read the disc (too far,
tilted, bars merged). No message means "not sure", not `bars_0`.

An answer is only published once it wins 3 of the last 5 frames, so
it already ignores a single bad frame.

If a bridge coaster is still on the cup, the counter sees a plain black
disc and reports `bars_0`.

name: pick a bar count

label: 6 · Compute Kit (drone only)
info: Servo, GPIO and the open-collector laser pulse on the DEXI Compute Kit. Hardware only: enable this tab on the aircraft.

name: Compute Kit
info: Hardware only. Enable this tab on the aircraft (double-click the tab and turn on Enabled).

name: Attach two servos to compute kit ports 0 and 1
Attach LED circuit to GPIO port 0
This assumes a KY-008 laser wired to the compute kit pin 15
KY-008 signal pin to 5V on compute kit, KY-008 negative pin to OC on compute kit
Shortest mission: 2 tags. Starts on the ground and takes off by itself.
Use it to learn the steps and for repeat testing: TAG HOP, then HOP BACK, then TAG HOP...
Full route: 5 tags in a row. Two ways to start, both join at 'center on tag 0':
START takes off by itself.  PILOT HAND-OFF: the pilot takes off by hand, hovers over tag 0 and flips the Offboard switch.
